test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
An athletic track forms a shape consisting of a rectangle with semicircles on two opposite ends. If the straight portions are each 100 metres long and the total perimeter of the track is 400 metres, what is the radius of each semicircular end (rounded off to two decimal places)?

 (Use pi = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total track = 2 straight + 2 semicircles ⇒ 2 × 100 + 2πr

⇒ 200 + 2πr = 400

⇒ 2πr = 200 ⇒ πr = 100

⇒ r = 100 ÷ (22/7)

**∴ r = 31.82 m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of straight portion = 100

Total perimeter = 400

π = 22 ÷ 7

**Formula used:**

Total perimeter = 2 × length + circumference of circle

Circumference of circle = 2 × π × r

 
 
 100 m 100 m r 

Two semicircles form one full circle

Curved length = 2πr

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total perimeter = 2 × 100 + 2 × π × r

⇒ 400 = 200 + 2 × π × r

⇒ 2 × π × r = 200

⇒ π × r = 100

⇒ r = 100 ÷ (22 ÷ 7)

⇒ r = 100 × 7 ÷ 22

⇒ r = 700 ÷ 22

⇒ r ≈ 31.82

**∴ The correct answer is 31.82 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Track Shape Concept

Two semicircles together form one complete circle.

Perimeter Formula

Perimeter = straight parts + curved parts.

π Approximation

Use π = 22/7 unless specified otherwise.
